title: Where you go, I will go

card.keepWhy: Ruth gathered it to feed Naomi, and that's where Boaz noticed her.
sources: Ruth 1:1-2 (a famine in the land; a man of Bethlehem goes to live in Moab with his wife Naomi and two sons)
Ruth 1:3-5 (Elimelech dies; the sons marry Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth; about ten years later both sons die, and Naomi is left without her two sons and her husband)
Ruth 1:6-8 (Naomi hears the Lord has given his people bread and sets out for home: “Go, return each of you to her mother’s house”)
Ruth 1:14 (they weep again; Orpah kisses her mother-in-law, but Ruth holds on to her)
Ruth 1:16-17 (“Where you go, I will go; and where you lodge, I will lodge; your people will be my people, and your God my God; where you die, I will die”)

Ruth 1:19-21 (the whole town is stirred, “Is this Naomi?” “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara; for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the Lord has brought me home again empty”)
Ruth 1:22 (they come to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest)
Ruth 2:1-3 (Boaz, a relative of Naomi’s husband; Ruth gleans after the reapers and happens on Boaz’s part of the field)
Ruth 2:11-16 (Boaz has heard all she did for her mother-in-law; at mealtime he gives her bread; he tells his young men to pull out some grain from the bundles for her on purpose)
Ruth 2:20 (Naomi: “Blessed be he by the Lord, who has not abandoned his kindness to the living and to the dead”)

Ruth 4:13-17 (Boaz marries Ruth; she bears a son; the women: “your daughter-in-law who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons”; Naomi lays the child in her lap; “A son is born to Naomi”; they name him Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David)
Leviticus 19:9-10, 23:22; Deuteronomy 24:19 (leave the edges and the gleanings of the harvest for the poor and the foreigner)
Matthew 1:5 (Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth, in the genealogy of Jesus)
Name meanings: Naomi, “pleasant”; Mara, “bitter” (Ruth 1:20 plays on both); Bethlehem, Hebrew Beit Lechem, “house of bread”
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized (the film’s narration, art/sacred/ruth/voice)
check: The film’s caption calls Boaz “a relative of Naomi”; Ruth 2:1 says a relative of her husband Elimelech (Naomi herself says “a close relative to us” in 2:20). Confirm the shorthand is acceptable.
The lesson leaves out chapter 3 (the threshing floor) and the nearer redeemer of chapter 4, to keep it light. Confirm the shortened arc is fair.
“They had nothing” (narration) is an interpretation of Naomi’s “brought me home again empty” (1:21). Confirm.
Bethlehem as “house of bread” is the common reading of Beit Lechem; some scholars propose other origins for the name. Confirm the match item’s wording.

The teach line calls hesed “loyal love” and says the story answers Naomi’s grief through people rather than a voice from heaven. Confirm this Christian framing (and the Matthew 1:5 link) reads well across Protestant traditions.
Place: the trip lands at the Shepherds’ Field outside Bethlehem (Beit Sahour); tradition, not the text, places Boaz’s fields there. The guide says so.
The narration voice is the stand-in narrator from ruth-film.html, not Denzel.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there someone you’re missing right now?
options: i’m so sorry. keep them close while you hear this one. the woman in it knew that ache.
then this one is for them too. watch who stays.
good. keep this one for a day you, or a friend, might need it.

steps.label: Ruth 1:3-5
steps.line: In the land of Moab, a woman named Naomi lost her husband, and then both of her sons.

steps.q: Naomi was from Bethlehem, not Moab. Why had her family left home years before?
o: A war had driven them out
There was a famine in the land
Her husband went to trade there
steps.why: Ruth 1:1: there was a famine. And Bethlehem means “house of bread.” A family left the house of bread because there was no bread.

steps.label: Ruth 1:6-8
steps.line: She decided to go home to Bethlehem. On the road, she told her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you, to your mother’s house.”

steps.label: Ruth 1:14
steps.line: They wept together. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, and went home.

steps.q: Naomi tells Ruth to go home too. What does Ruth do?
o: Walks a little way, then turns back
steps.why: She holds on. And she says one of the most famous lines in the Bible.

steps.pre: “Where you go, I will go. Your people will be my people, and your
steps.why: “Your God my God.” Ruth, a woman of Moab, wasn’t only choosing Naomi. She was choosing Naomi’s God too.

steps.label: Ruth 1:16
steps.line: But Ruth held on to her. “Where you go, I will go. Where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.”

steps.label: Ruth 1:19, 22
steps.line: So the two of them came to Bethlehem, just as the barley harvest began. They had nothing.

steps.label: Ruth 1:19-21
steps.line: The whole town came out: “Is this Naomi?” She said, “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara. I went away full, and the Lord has brought me home empty.”

steps.q: Naomi means “pleasant.” What does Mara, the name she asks for, mean?
steps.why: Bitter. “The Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me,” she says (Ruth 1:20). She says it out loud, about God, and nobody in the story tells her to cheer up.

steps.label: Ruth 2:2-3
steps.line: Ruth went out to the fields to gather the grain the harvesters left behind, to feed them both.

steps.q: Ruth was a foreigner with nothing. Why was she allowed to gather grain in someone else’s field?
o: The harvest was over, so it was free
The law said leave some for the poor
steps.why: Leviticus 19:9-10 and Deuteronomy 24:19: leave the edges and the dropped grain for the poor and the foreigner. A safety net, built into every harvest.

steps.label: Ruth 2:1-3, 15-16
steps.line: The field belonged to Boaz, a relative of Naomi. He noticed her, and told his workers to leave extra grain for her on purpose.

steps.label: Ruth 2:11, 14
steps.line: At mealtime he shared his bread with her. He had heard how she stood by Naomi.

steps.q: Ruth comes home with a big bundle of barley and says whose field it was. What does “bitter” Naomi say?
o: “May the Lord bless him. His kindness hasn’t stopped.”
steps.why: Ruth 2:20: “Blessed be he by the Lord, who has not abandoned his kindness to the living and to the dead.” Her first blessing since she came home bitter.

steps.label: Ruth 4:13
steps.line: Boaz married Ruth, and they had a son. They named him Obed.

steps.label: Ruth 4:16-17
steps.line: Naomi held the child in her arms, and the women of the town said, “A son is born to Naomi.” That boy became the grandfather of King David.

steps.q: In this story the names do some of the talking. Match them.
steps.why: Pleasant turned bitter, then held a grandson. And the house of bread had bread again, at barley harvest.

say: here’s what i love. naomi told the whole town god had made her life bitter, and the bible keeps her words. no one tells her to cheer up.

the answer didn’t come as a voice from the sky. it came through people: a daughter-in-law who wouldn’t leave, a farmer who left extra grain on purpose. the hebrew word is hesed, loyal love that keeps showing up.
and christians meet ruth again on the first page of the new testament. matthew names her, an outsider from moab, in the family tree of jesus.

steps.q: Naomi’s grief didn’t vanish in a day. What carried her from “call me Mara” to a baby in her arms?
o: She decided to stop feeling sad
Loyal love from the people who stayed
A prophet told her God had forgiven her
steps.why: Ruth stayed, Boaz made room, and the women of the town said Ruth was “better to you than seven sons” (Ruth 4:15). God’s kindness came wearing ordinary faces.

today.say: missing someone is heavy, and you don’t have to carry it alone. today, let one person in: tell a friend who you’re missing. or be someone’s ruth, and just show up. if you’d like, tell god honestly how it feels, the way naomi did. your choice.
options: that’s brave. ruth didn’t fix naomi’s grief. she stayed. let someone stay.
be their ruth. no speech needed. just come, and bring bread if you can.
